passages.text: So King Solomon ruled over Israel, and these were his chief officials: Azariah son of Zadok was the priest; Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, were secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the army; Zadok and Abiathar were priests; Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the governors; Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and adviser to the king; Ahishar was in charge of the palace; and Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of the forced labor.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled over all Israel.
He had several chief officials.
Azariah was the son of Zadok.
Azariah was the priest.
Elihoreph and Ahijah were sons of Shisha.
Elihoreph and Ahijah were secretaries.
Jehoshaphat was the son of Ahilud.
Jehoshaphat was the recorder.
Benaiah was the son of Jehoiada.
Benaiah was in charge of the army.
Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
Azariah was the son of Nathan.
Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the governors.
Zabud was the son of Nathan.
Zabud was a priest.
Zabud was an adviser to the king.
Ahishar was in charge of the palace.
Adoniram was the son of Abda.
Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס וְאֵ֥לֶּה הַשָּׂרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁר־ ל֑וֹ עֲזַרְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־ צָד֖וֹק הַכֹּהֵֽן׃ס אֱלִיחֹ֧רֶף וַאֲחִיָּ֛ה בְּנֵ֥י שִׁישָׁ֖א סֹפְרִ֑ים יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בֶּן־ אֲחִיל֖וּד הַמַּזְכִּֽיר׃ וּבְנָיָ֥הוּ בֶן־ יְהוֹיָדָ֖ע עַל־ הַצָּבָ֑א וְצָד֥וֹק וְאֶבְיָתָ֖ר כֹּהֲנִֽים׃ס וַעֲזַרְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־ נָתָ֖ן עַל־ הַנִּצָּבִ֑ים וְזָב֧וּד בֶּן־ נָתָ֛ן כֹּהֵ֖ן רֵעֶ֥ה הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ וַאֲחִישָׁ֖ר עַל־ הַבָּ֑יִת וַאֲדֹנִירָ֥ם בֶּן־ עַבְדָּ֖א עַל־ הַמַּֽס׃ס

passages.text: Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel to provide food for the king and his household. Each one would arrange provisions for one month of the year, and these were their names: Ben-hur in the hill country of Ephraim; Ben-deker in Makaz, in Shaalbim, in Beth-shemesh, and in Elon-beth-hanan; Ben-hesed in Arubboth (Socoh and all the land of Hepher belonged to him); Ben-abinadab in Naphath-dor (Taphath, a daughter of Solomon, was his wife); Baana son of Ahilud in Taanach, in Megiddo, and in all of Beth-shean next to Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and on past Jokmeam; Ben-geber in Ramoth-gilead (the villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead belonged to him, as well as the region of Argob in Bashan with its sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars); Ahinadab son of Iddo in Mahanaim; Ahimaaz in Naphtali (he had married Basemath, a daughter of Solomon); Baana son of Hushai in Asher and in Aloth; Jehoshaphat son of Paruah in Issachar; Shimei son of Ela in Benjamin; Geber son of Uri in the land of Gilead, including the territories of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan. There was also one governor in the land of Judah.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled over all Israel.
He appointed twelve governors over the nation.
These governors provided food for the king and his household.
Each governor supplied provisions for one month of the year.
Here are their names and regions:
Ben-hur was in the hill country of Ephraim.
Ben-deker was in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan.
Ben-hesed was in Arubboth.
Socoh and all the land of Hepher belonged to Ben-hesed.
Ben-abinadab was in Naphath-dor.
Taphath, a daughter of Solomon, was the wife of Ben-abinadab.
Baana son of Ahilud was in Taanach, in Megiddo, and in all of Beth-shean next to Zarethan below Jezreel.
His region stretched from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and on past Jokmeam.
Ben-geber was in Ramoth-gilead.
The villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead belonged to Ben-geber.
The region of Argob in Bashan also belonged to him.
This region had sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars.
Ahinadab son of Iddo was in Mahanaim.
Ahimaaz was in Naphtali.
Ahimaaz married Basemath, a daughter of Solomon.
Baana son of Hushai was in Asher and in Aloth.
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was in Issachar.
Shimei son of Ela was in Benjamin.
Geber son of Uri was in the land of Gilead.
This included the territories of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan.
There was also one governor in the land of Judah.
passages.original: וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֞ה שְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֤ר נִצָּבִים֙ עַל־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְכִלְכְּל֥וּ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְאֶת־ בֵּית֑וֹ חֹ֧דֶשׁ בַּשָּׁנָ֛ה יִהְיֶ֥ה עַל־ אֶחָד לְכַלְכֵּֽל׃ס וְאֵ֣לֶּה שְׁמוֹתָ֔ם בֶּן־ ח֖וּר בְּהַ֥ר אֶפְרָֽיִם׃ס בֶּן־ דֶּ֛קֶר בְּמָקַ֥ץ וּבְשַֽׁעַלְבִ֖ים וּבֵ֣ית שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וְאֵיל֖וֹן בֵּ֥ית חָנָֽן׃ס בֶּן־ חֶ֖סֶד בָּֽאֲרֻבּ֑וֹת ל֥וֹ שֹׂכֹ֖ה וְכָל־ אֶ֥רֶץ חֵֽפֶר׃ס בֶּן־ אֲבִֽינָדָ֖ב כָּל־ נָ֣פַת דֹּ֑אר טָפַת֙ בַּת־ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה הָ֥יְתָה לּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃ס בַּֽעֲנָא֙ בֶּן־ אֲחִיל֔וּד תַּעְנַ֖ךְ וּמְגִדּ֑וֹ וְכָל־ בֵּ֣ית שְׁאָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ אֵ֨צֶל צָרְתַ֜נָה מִתַּ֣חַת לְיִזְרְעֶ֗אל מִבֵּ֤ית שְׁאָן֙ עַ֚ד אָבֵ֣ל מְחוֹלָ֔ה עַ֖ד מֵעֵ֥בֶר לְיָקְמֳעָֽם׃ס בֶּן־ גֶּ֖בֶר בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד ל֡וֹ חַוֺּת֩ יָאִ֨יר בֶּן־ מְנַשֶּׁ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּגִּלְעָ֗ד ל֚וֹ חֶ֤בֶל אַרְגֹּב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּבָּשָׁ֔ן שִׁשִּׁים֙ עָרִ֣ים גְּדֹל֔וֹת חוֹמָ֖ה וּבְרִ֥יחַ נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃ס אֲחִֽינָדָ֥ב בֶּן־ עִדֹּ֖א מַחֲנָֽיְמָה׃ אֲחִימַ֖עַץ בְּנַפְתָּלִ֑י גַּם־ ה֗וּא לָקַ֛ח אֶת־ בָּשְׂמַ֥ת בַּת־ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְאִשָּֽׁה׃ בַּֽעֲנָא֙ בֶּן־ חוּשָׁ֔י בְּאָשֵׁ֖ר וּבְעָלֽוֹת׃ס יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בֶּן־ פָּר֖וּחַ בְּיִשָׂשכָֽר׃ס שִׁמְעִ֥י בֶן־ אֵלָ֖א בְּבִנְיָמִֽן׃ס גֶּ֥בֶר בֶּן־ אֻרִ֖י בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גִּלְעָ֑ד אֶ֜רֶץ סִיח֣וֹן׀ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֗י וְעֹג֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֔ן וּנְצִ֥יב אֶחָ֖ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore, and they were eating and drinking and rejoicing.
passages.sermon:
Judah and Israel were two tribes of God's people.
The people of Judah and Israel were very many.
They were as numerous as the sand on the seashore.
They ate.
They drank.
They rejoiced.
passages.original: יְהוּדָ֤ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ רַבִּ֔ים כַּח֥וֹל אֲשֶׁר־ עַל־ הַיָּ֖ם לָרֹ֑ב אֹכְלִ֥ים וְשֹׁתִ֖ים וּשְׂמֵחִֽים׃

passages.text: And Solomon reigned over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt. These kingdoms offered tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king over many kingdoms.
He ruled from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines.
His rule reached as far as the border of Egypt.
All these kingdoms brought tribute to Solomon.
They served Solomon throughout his life.
passages.original: וּשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה הָיָ֤ה מוֹשֵׁל֙ בְּכָל־ הַמַּמְלָכ֔וֹת מִן־ הַנָּהָר֙ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְעַ֖ד גְּב֣וּל מִצְרָ֑יִם מַגִּשִׁ֥ים מִנְחָ֛ה וְעֹבְדִ֥ים אֶת־ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה כָּל־ יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו׃פ

passages.text: Solomon’s provisions for a single day were thirty cors of fine flour, sixty cors of meal, ten fat oxen, twenty range oxen, and a hundred sheep, as well as deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened poultry.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king over Israel and Judah.
Solomon received large daily provisions.
Each day, Solomon had thirty cors of fine flour.
Each day, Solomon had sixty cors of meal.
Each day, Solomon had ten fat oxen.
Each day, Solomon had twenty pasture oxen.
Each day, Solomon had one hundred sheep.
Solomon also received deer.
Solomon also received gazelles.
Solomon also received roebucks.
Solomon also received fattened poultry.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י לֶֽחֶם־ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְי֣וֹם אֶחָ֑ד שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים כֹּר֙ סֹ֔לֶת וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים כֹּ֖ר קָֽמַח׃ עֲשָׂרָ֨ה בָקָ֜ר בְּרִאִ֗ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים בָּקָ֛ר רְעִ֖י וּמֵ֣אָה צֹ֑אן לְ֠בַד מֵֽאַיָּ֤ל וּצְבִי֙ וְיַחְמ֔וּר וּבַרְבֻּרִ֖ים אֲבוּסִֽים׃

passages.text: For Solomon had dominion over everything west of the Euphrates —over all the kingdoms from Tiphsah to Gaza—and he had peace on all sides.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king.
He ruled over everything west of the Euphrates River.
He ruled from Tiphsah to Gaza.
He ruled over all the kingdoms in that region.
Solomon had peace on every side.
passages.original: כִּי־ ה֞וּא רֹדֶ֣ה׀ בְּכָל־ עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֗ר מִתִּפְסַח֙ וְעַד־ עַזָּ֔ה בְּכָל־ מַלְכֵ֖י עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֑ר וְשָׁל֗וֹם הָ֥יָה ל֛וֹ מִכָּל־ עֲבָרָ֖יו מִסָּבִֽיב׃

passages.text: Throughout the days of Solomon, Judah and Israel dwelt securely from Dan to Beersheba, each man under his own vine and his own fig tree.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king over Israel and Judah.
He ruled during a time of peace and safety.
Judah and Israel lived securely.
They lived in safety from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
Every man had his own vine.
Every man had his own fig tree.
This peace lasted all the days of Solomon.
passages.original: וַיֵּשֶׁב֩ יְהוּדָ֨ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לָבֶ֗טַח אִ֣ישׁ תַּ֤חַת גַּפְנוֹ֙ וְתַ֣חַת תְּאֵֽנָת֔וֹ מִדָּ֖ן וְעַד־ בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃ס

passages.text: Solomon had 4,000 stalls for his chariot horses and 12,000 horses.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king over Israel and Judah.
Solomon ruled in a time of peace and security.
Solomon had great wealth and resources.
Solomon owned 4,000 stalls for his chariot horses.
Solomon had 12,000 horses.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י לִשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אֻרְוֺ֥ת סוּסִ֖ים לְמֶרְכָּב֑וֹ וּשְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: Each month the governors in turn provided food for King Solomon and all who came to his table. They saw to it that nothing was lacking.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the ruler of Israel.
\r\nHe had many people who served him.
\r\nThe governors were responsible for providing food.
\r\nEach governor took a turn every month.
\r\nThey gave food to King Solomon.
\r\nThey also gave food to everyone who ate at King Solomon’s table.
\r\nThey made sure nothing was missing.
\r\nNo one lacked anything.
passages.original: וְכִלְכְּלוּ֩ הַנִּצָּבִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה אֶת־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה וְאֵ֧ת כָּל־ הַקָּרֵ֛ב אֶל־ שֻׁלְחַ֥ן הַמֶּֽלֶךְ־ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ חָדְשׁ֑וֹ לֹ֥א יְעַדְּר֖וּ דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: Each one also brought to the required place their quotas of barley and straw for the chariot horses and other horses.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king of Israel.
He had many chariot horses and other horses.
Each governor had a duty.
Each governor brought barley and straw.
They brought these for the chariot horses and other horses.
They brought the barley and straw to the required place.
Each man brought his share as he was assigned.
passages.original: וְהַשְּׂעֹרִ֣ים וְהַתֶּ֔בֶן לַסּוּסִ֖ים וְלָרָ֑כֶשׁ יָבִ֗אוּ אֶל־ הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִֽהְיֶה־ שָּׁ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ כְּמִשְׁפָּטֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: And God gave Solomon wisdom, exceedingly deep insight, and understanding beyond measure, like the sand on the seashore.
passages.sermon:
God gave Solomon wisdom.
God gave Solomon very great insight.
God gave Solomon understanding that was beyond measure.
Solomon’s understanding was as vast as the sand on the seashore.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּן֩ אֱלֹהִ֨ים חָכְמָ֧ה לִשְׁלֹמֹ֛ה וּתְבוּנָ֖ה הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וְרֹ֣חַב לֵ֔ב כַּח֕וֹל אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ שְׂפַ֥ת הַיָּֽם׃

passages.text: Solomon’s wisdom was greater than that of all the men of the East, greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was a king of Israel.
God gave Solomon great wisdom.
Solomon’s wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the men of the East.
Solomon’s wisdom was greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֙רֶב֙ חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מֵֽחָכְמַ֖ת כָּל־ בְּנֵי־ קֶ֑דֶם וּמִכֹּ֖ל חָכְמַ֥ת מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: He was wiser than all men—wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and wiser than Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. And his fame spread throughout the surrounding nations.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was a king of Israel.
God gave Solomon great wisdom.
Solomon was wiser than all other men.
He was wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite.
He was wiser than Heman.
He was wiser than Calcol.
He was wiser than Darda.
Calcol and Darda were sons of Mahol.
People in all the surrounding nations heard about Solomon.
Solomon became famous everywhere around Israel.
passages.original: וַיֶּחְכַּם֮ מִכָּל־ הָֽאָדָם֒ מֵאֵיתָ֣ן הָאֶזְרָחִ֗י וְהֵימָ֧ן וְכַלְכֹּ֛ל וְדַרְדַּ֖ע בְּנֵ֣י מָח֑וֹל וַיְהִֽי־ שְׁמ֥וֹ בְכָֽל־ הַגּוֹיִ֖ם סָבִֽיב׃

passages.text: Solomon composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was a king of Israel.
God gave Solomon great wisdom.
Solomon spoke three thousand proverbs.
Solomon wrote one thousand and five songs.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֕ר שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים מָשָׁ֑ל וַיְהִ֥י שִׁיר֖וֹ חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה וָאָֽלֶף׃

passages.text: He spoke of trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing in the wall, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was a king of Israel.
God gave Solomon great wisdom.
Solomon spoke about trees.
He spoke about the cedar tree in Lebanon.
He spoke about the hyssop plant that grows in the wall.
Solomon also spoke about animals.
He spoke about birds.
He spoke about reptiles.
He spoke about fish.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּר֮ עַל־ הָֽעֵצִים֒ מִן־ הָאֶ֙רֶז֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלְּבָנ֔וֹן וְעַד֙ הָאֵז֔וֹב אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֹצֵ֖א בַּקִּ֑יר וַיְדַבֵּר֙ עַל־ הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה וְעַל־ הָע֔וֹף וְעַל־ הָרֶ֖מֶשׂ וְעַל־ הַדָּגִֽים׃

passages.text: So men of all nations came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was the king of Israel.
God gave Solomon great wisdom.
People from every nation heard about Solomon’s wisdom.
All the kings of the earth heard about Solomon’s wisdom.
These kings sent men to Solomon.
Men from all nations came to Solomon.
They came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ מִכָּל־ הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים לִשְׁמֹ֕עַ אֵ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה מֵאֵת֙ כָּל־ מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמְע֖וּ אֶת־ חָכְמָתֽוֹ׃ס
